To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
VEGF family member, VEGF-D, is expressed in lung tissue, with high expression during late fetal development.
VEGF-C, -D, and -F are expressed in embryonic mouse lung and that VEGF-A and VEGF-C expression is upregulated in the adult lung after lung injury.
vegf-d mRNA was found in high levels in the developing mouse lung and at lower levels in other tissues, including the adult lung.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression pattern of the newly identified VEGF-D in mouse lung.
the identification, isolation and characterization of novel angiogenic growth factors, and their receptors, and their expression in normal and pathological tissues.
the identification of novel endothelial growth factors and the elucidation of their role in the development and physiology of the vascular system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
VEGF is the most important angiogenic factor in the developing embryo, while VEGF-C, -D and VEGF-B may be more important in the adult.
the vegf-d gene expression is restricted to the lung tissue and is up-regulated prior to birth.
VEGF-C is expressed in lymphatic vessels and VEGF-A, VEGF-B, VEGF-D, VEGF-E and PIGF are expressed in blood vessels, and VEGF-C, VEGF-A and VEGF-F in the embryonic and/or adult heart.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
VEGF-A, B, C and D may be involved in angiogenesis, but VEGF-A seems to be the most important.
VEGF-A is the most important angiogenic factor, VEGF-B and VEGF-C have a more restricted role and VEGF- D is mainly expressed in lung tissue during the fetal period.
vegf-d is expressed in lung tissue, and is most abundant at the end of the fetal period.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the VEGF-D gene is highly expressed during fetal lung development and is restricted to the adult lung.
vegf-d is a gene with a very limited expression pattern in adult and fetal mouse, which is mainly restricted to the embryonic lung.
the expression of the vegf-d gene is highly restricted in adult mouse tissues, and that its expression is upregulated in embryonic lung during late fetal development.
